subject: Next steps: deployment mode + compliance requirements for MediHealth
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: deployment mode + compliance requirements for MediHealth

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the path forward: 

Summary of your requirements (as I understood them):
- PHI/HIPAA scope: model inputs and outputs will include patient-identifiable info; MediHealth needs a signed BAA and evidence of controls.
- SOC 2: your procurement team needs the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary of relevant controls (encryption at rest, access logging, change control).
- Network constraints: preference for private VPC peering or on-prem for production; POC can run on Hosted but must use encryption and data minimization.
- Timeline: POC in April, production decision in May.

Recommended deployment approach:
1) POC: Hosted API with dedicated tenant + strict request-level opt-out of persistent logs (fastest to start).
2) Pre-prod/Validation: Redwood Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) inside a customer VPC - gives predictable throughput and stronger isolation.
3) Production: Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) if you require full network isolation and customer-managed KMS for PHI.

Immediate next steps:
- I will send our SOC 2 snapshot and a BAA draft (attached) for your security team to review.
- Vivek will follow up with a high-level Dedicated vs Private pricing delta and capacity sizing worksheet.
- Marissa will prepare a short SRE note on KV cache handling and data retention configs for PHI-sensitive workload.
- Lisa: confirm whether the initial POC can use Hosted API for up to 30 days while we set up Dedicated.

If that's all accurate, we'll target a short alignment call next week with your InfoSec.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter

Hi Ben — thanks, that summary is helpful and matches the conversation. A few clarifications from InfoSec's side: 

- BAA: We need a first pass to circulate internally; can you confirm whether Redwood's hosted logs are encrypted and retained for how long by default?
- SOC 2: please include the period covered by the report and whether the report includes data center providers we use (GCP us-west2).
- Private deployment: our network team is specifically asking about IPsec vs VPC peering options and whether Redwood supports HSM-based customer-managed keys.

POC note: We prefer the POC to run against a Dedicated pool if the timeline allows, but we understand Hosted is faster. If Dedicated setup will push POC past mid-April, we can start on Hosted with strict log controls.

Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow with Vivek and your SRE to walk the security checklist?

Thanks — Lisa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment mode + compliance requirements for MediHealth

Hi Lisa — great to meet briefly on the call earlier. Quick answers while I pull together a more detailed pricing/size estimate: 

- Logs & retention (Hosted): by default we persist request/response logs for 30 days; we can enable an enterprise opt-out for persistent logging on a per-tenant basis during POC (no retention). All logs are encrypted at rest and in transit using AES-256 and TLS 1.3 respectively.
- SOC 2 report: Ben, attaching the snapshot should show the audit period (FY2025) and the scope; we operate on GCP and include our major cloud partners in the attestation.
- Private KMS/HSM: yes — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (bring-your-own-key).
- Networking: we support both VPC peering (recommended for lower ops) and IPsec tunnels for on-prem connectivity. VPC peering is generally easier for cloud-to-cloud setups.

POC recommendation: If your procurement schedule is tight, start POC on Hosted with the logging opt-out. If you need realistic production throughput testing, we should provision a small Dedicated pool — provisioning lead time is ~2 weeks after contract signature.

I'll send a short capacity worksheet and a 2-line pricing delta (Dedicated vs Private) by EOD. Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync tomorrow at 11am PT (Marissa will cover SRE specifics)?

— Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment mode + compliance requirements for MediHealth

Hi Lisa — quick SRE note for your team before tomorrow's sync: 

- KV cache & PHI: we can enable strict prefix scoping and in-memory-only caches for PHI-sensitive routes. No PHI is written to disk in those configs.
- Retention controls: we support per-route retention policies; for POC set to 0 days (no persistent logs) and for pre-prod set to 7 days.
- Audit logs: request-level audit logs (who/when/which model/size) are available and can be pushed to your SIEM via secure delivery (syslog/Cloud PubSub).
- Performance impact: Dedicated pool will reduce tail latency variance for long sequences; expect ~15-20% latency improvement on 8k-context requests vs Hosted multitenant.

I attached a network sketch and will bring a short slide to the tech sync.

Cheers — Marissa

Marissa Cole

Thanks all — couple of follow-ups from our side after reviewing the SOC snapshot and BAA draft: 

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated offering has dedicated tenancy at the hypervisor level or if it's dedicated instances within a shared control plane? We need to document the isolation model.
2) For the BAA: section 4.2 on subcontractors — please provide the list of sub-processors handling PHI (if any).
3) Can you provide an example key rotation policy for customer-managed KMS? We need to align policies with our internal audit timeline.

We are available for the technical sync tomorrow at 11am PT. Please send the calendar invite and include any meeting notes after the call.

Regards — MediHealth InfoSec

— InfoSec Team

Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment mode + compliance requirements for MediHealth

Thanks for the questions — captured and responded inline: 

1) Dedicated tenancy: Redwood Dedicated provides dedicated GPU pools (compute tenancy) with a dedicated control plane partitioning. Hypervisor-level tenancy depends on customer safety requirements; for customers requiring hypervisor separation we offer Private on-prem installs or single-tenant VPC appliances.

2) Sub-processors: list included in the SOC snapshot appendix (GCP, CloudStorage vendor, CDN partner). We'll extract a short sub-processor list and add to the BAA draft for section 4.2.

3) Key rotation policy: attached is a one-page example: we recommend 90-day rotation for KMS keys used for ephemeral tokens and annual rotation for long-lived CMKs; all rotations are logged and can trigger rekey windows that we coordinate with your ops team.

Action items I am closing out now: 
- Attach updated BAA draft with subprocessors (Monica to manage DocX redline).
- Vivek: send Dedicated vs Private cost delta and capacity worksheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Marissa: include sample retention config and audit log delivery steps in the tech sync slide deck.

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 11am sync and drop meeting notes after. Appreciate the team's detailed review — talk tomorrow.

Best — Ben
